rich_summary: In this section, Duryodhana defiantly refuses Krishna’s plea for peace and denies any wrongdoing toward the Pandavas. He argues that the Kshatriya code demands unwavering pride in battle and declares he would rather die on a bed of arrows than submit. Most famously, he swears he will not grant the Pandavas even land equal to the tip of a needle. Krishna responds with fierce anger, listing Duryodhana’s many crimes: the rigged dice game, the humiliation of Draupadi, attempts to burn the Pandavas alive, and repeated plots to kill them. He condemns Duryodhana’s refusal to restore their rightful share and warns that war and destruction will follow. The confrontation reveals the moral divide—Krishna representing justice and memory of wrongs, while Duryodhana embodies pride, denial, and the stubborn resolve that makes the coming war inevitable.

highlight_spans.why: Duryodhana questions why the Pandavas consider the Kauravas enemies, framing the conflict through his self‑justifying perspective.
The speech on Kshatriya duty—better to die on a bed of arrows than bow—captures the warrior ethos driving Duryodhana’s refusal to compromise.
Duryodhana’s uncompromising declaration that not even land the size of a needle’s tip will be given to the Pandavas—one of the most famous lines signaling the inevitability of war.
Krishna angrily recounts the humiliation of Draupadi and other injustices, emotionally indicting Duryodhana before the court.
Krishna lists Duryodhana’s past crimes—poisoning, burning the Pandavas, deceit at dice—forming the moral case for the Pandavas’ claim and the coming conflict.

top_scenes.scene_text: Duryodhana standing defiantly in the Kuru court before Krishna and the assembled elders, proclaiming he will not yield even land the size of a needle’s tip.
Krishna with eyes blazing in anger, pointing at Duryodhana while recounting the humiliation of Draupadi before the shocked Kuru assembly.
Duryodhana rising like a furious serpent and storming out of the royal court while Bhishma, Drona, Vidura, and Dhritarashtra watch in grave silence.
